summary: A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Wolfgang Morgenroth earned his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild (~1953–1958). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1976–1992) and the University of Potsdam (2020).

Wolfram Eberhard worked in sinology and history/archaeology after studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1927–1933). He held posts at Ankara University (~1937–1948) and as professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1948–1976).
Specializing in religious and Buddhist studies, Woncheol Yun earned a PhD at Stony Brook University. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University, attested in 2012.

Woosung Huh works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hawaii and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

Wu Hung, a specialist in history, archaeology, and sinology, studied at Harvard University (~1980–1987). From around 1994, he held posts at the Smart Museum of Art and as Professor at the University of Chicago.
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His traditional teachers included Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.

Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016). Xianda studied under K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Xianlin Ji specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, studying at Tsinghua University (1930–1934) and the University of Göttingen (1935–1941). He held posts at Göttingen (1937) and Peking University (1946; Life Professor 1980).

Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and Indology, holding positions at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1947), Peking University (~1949–1953), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977 as professor), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995 as professor).
Xiaoting Wei specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. Wei earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng-Mei Ku, attested in 2004.
Xinchuan Huang studied at Peking University (~1954–1958) and worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Huang held a post as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977).

Xinru Liu, a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–1985). Liu taught at The College of New Jersey (~2002) and held posts at CASS (attested 2010).
Xiuzhi Zeng, who works in Buddhist and religious studies, completed an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen, attested in 2006.

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008) and held an associate professor post at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011) and a Research Associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017).

Y. Karunadasa studied at SOAS, University of London under David Friedman (~1960–1963) in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Karunadasa served as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1990–2000, 2008) and Professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2013).

Yael Bentor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University under Gregory Schopen and other scholars. Bentor taught in the Department of Indian Studies at Hebrew University (attested 2000).
Yanfei Zhou is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the doctoral supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An specializes in Buddhist studies. An studied under Hojin (attested 2003) and completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich by 1998.
Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetology scholar who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Henry Y. H. Zhao (~1999–2004).
